summary: Format-dispatch helper for CRT-style float-to-string conversion. Inspects the format code argument a3 and selects one of three conversion helpers: for ASCII 'e'/'E' (101/69) calls FloatToStringWithSignWidth(a1, a2, a4, a5) (exponent/scientific form); for ASCII 'f' (102) calls IntToStringWithSignPositionDraw(a1, a2, a4); otherwise falls through to the default UtilityFunction_bfec(a1, a2, a4, a5). Returns the pointer (to the resulting string buffer) produced by whichever helper ran. Owning object unknown.

local_names.a1: double source value to convert (may be cast to int on the int path)
local_names.a2: destination character buffer for the formatted string
local_names.a4: numeric argument forwarded to the selected helper (e.g. width)
local_names.a5: numeric argument forwarded to the selected helper

operations.description: Guard: when a3 == 101 ('e') or a3 == 69 ('E'), take the scientific/exponent float-to-string path and return its result immediately.
Call FloatToStringWithSignWidth(a1, (int)a2, a4, a5) which formats the double a1 into the buffer a2 with sign/width handling; its returned pointer becomes the function result.
Guard: when a3 == 102 ('f'), take the fixed-point int-with-sign path and return its result immediately.
Call IntToStringWithSignPositionDraw(a1, (int)a2, a4) which formats with sign and position (fixed) semantics; its returned pointer becomes the function result.
Fallback path: call UtilityFunction_bfec(a1, a2, a4, a5) for any format code other than 'e'/'E'/'f'; its returned pointer becomes the function result.
Return the pointer produced by the selected conversion helper.
